svg.text: PROPOSED: operator-owned Workload for a Dynamic Allocation SparkApplication
Architecture A — apache/spark-kubernetes-operator + Pradeep39/kueue · lane tint and sublabel give the deployment side; sublabel also gives change status

g.text: Spark driver pod / kube control plane

svg.text: Precondition, and the first thing that has to be built: the executor pod template must already carry
kueue.x-k8s.io/elastic-job as a scheduling gate, plus the PodSet label and the workload-slice-name annotation. In
the Kueue-owned design a Kueue webhook injects these. Here no Kueue webhook sees the CR, so the OPERATOR must inject
them when it builds the executor pod template. Without the gate there is no admission control at all: the driver
creates executors and kube-scheduler places them.
create executor Pods (must be born gated)
Executor Pods are owned by the DRIVER Pod, so
there is no OwnerReference chain to watch
List Pods by app-name + spark-role label
ones. Excluding gated Pods deadlocks scale-up
lower bound stops a mid-startup reconcile
annotations. Without them Kueue sees unrelated
Workloads: no predecessor, no delta charging,
The load-bearing CHANGE. requestAdmission today returns early once the Workload is admitted, and its only reaction
to a changed podSet is to DELETE and recreate it while still pending. Neither is the slice protocol. It has to
create a new Workload slice that names its predecessor, and leave the predecessor in place for the scheduler.
Annotation-driven, so this works unchanged for
the DELTA vs the replaced slice
only the chain tip. Key is namespace + slice
name + owning job UID, so the ownerReference
alreadyUngated. Reads the PodSet label and
slice annotation OFF THE PODS, which is why
remove the gate from exactly `room` Pods;
Scale-down is deliberately not drawn. It is two in-place patches - spec.podSets[].count and status.admission - and
the second is only permitted by the decrease-only, elastic-only exception in Kueue's own workload webhook. That
exception is KUEUE-side and cannot be delivered from the operator, so this architecture is not completable
operator-side alone. Delete-and-recreate is not a substitute: it drops the predecessor the scheduler needs in order
